summary.one_liner: BeeBot is an experimental autonomous AI assistant meant to carry out a wide range of practical tasks on its own, currently on hold due to LLM limitations.
summary.what_it_does: BeeBot is a Python project (managed with poetry) that aims to act as a personal autonomous assistant. It selects tools through AutoPack, which it also uses as its tool package manager, and can acquire additional tools during task execution. It offers a CLI (`poetry run beebot`) and a REST API conforming to the e2b standard, where tasks are created with a text input and advanced one step at a time. It has a websocket endpoint intended to publish events, though the README says notifications are being reworked and may not work. Persistence is described as required, with SQLite supported and Postgres recommended via docker compose. The filesystem layer is swappable between in-memory, on-disk, or database storage, and Helicone caching is available if enabled. The README states that development is currently on hold.
use_cases: Experimenting with autonomous AI task execution
Creating and stepping through tasks via a REST API
Running an LLM agent that writes files to a workspace
Studying tool-selection approaches for LLM agents
how_to_run: docker compose up -d (to start Postgres for persistence)
notable: Tool selection and runtime tool acquisition via AutoPack
REST API following the e2b standard
Swappable filesystem emulation (in-memory, on-disk, or database)
Dynamic manipulation of task history during execution
Uses end-to-end tests instead of unit tests, by stated design
caveats: Development is on hold; the author says current LLMs are not up to generalized autonomous tasks (late 2023)
Persistence is required; Postgres via Docker is recommended over SQLite
Websocket notifications are being reworked and may not work; web UI is not yet available
keywords: run ai to do tasks for me
